Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 371 of 2024
Applicant :- Arvind Parashar

Counsel for Applicant :- Mohammad Fateh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Applicant has filed this application under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the charge sheet dated 19.07.2014 as well as summoning order dated 02.01.2015 in Criminal Case No.
25 of 2015; titled State vs. Arvind Prashar, arising out of Case Crime No. 20 of 2013, under Sections 376 and 420 IPC, Police Station Devraniya, District Bareilly, pending before the Judicial Magistrate,
Bahedi, District Bareilly and the entire proceedings arising therefrom.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was not aware of the pending impugned proceedings against him as he is serving in the Army and is posted at Chandigarh,
therefore, the delay has occurred in approaching this Court to challenge the impugned charge sheet dated 19.7.2014 filed in Case Crime No. 20 of 2013, under Sections 376 and 420 IPC.

He submits that the allegations in the First Information Report levelled by the complainant/opposite party no. 2 relates to the breach of promise of marriage between applicant and the complainant allegedly fixed for 27.2.2010, but the same was never solemnized.

He submits that the plot which was given to the applicant by the father of the complainant in the year 2010 has been returned to him, and in this regard, learned counsel has drawn the attention of the Court to the statement of the complainant and her father recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
According to the learned counsel, the continuation of proceedings against applicant is misuse of process of law, therefore, he prays for quashing of the impugned proceedings.

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel and considering his submissions, this Court finds that according to the prosecution, immediately after fixation of marriage of the applicant with complainant, the plot was given by the father of the complainant to the applicant in the year 2010 and the applicant has claimed to have returned the said immovable property, as their wedding did not take place, and thereafter, the applicant solemnized the marriage with another girl in the year 2013.

Further, a perusal of the zimni orders passed by the trial court would show that the trial court is continuously issuing arrest warrants against the applicant, but the applicant has not appeared before the trial court.
Thus, it cannot be believed that the applicant was not aware of the criminal proceedings initiated by the complainant.

Resultantly, considering the conduct of the applicant as well as delay in filing the application, this Court is not inclined to exercise inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
The application is dismissed.

Order Date :- 16.2.2024/Brijesh  Arvind Parashar vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78408941/
